observations: A tall, thin figure with elongated limbs stands against a flat teal ground; the left arm curves outward in a wide arc while the right arm drops low, creating an asymmetric silhouette.
Orange and blue dominate the figure's surface in overlapping bands, with white lines tracing the outer edges of limbs and a cluster of red circular marks at the small head in the upper right.
Yellow spikes radiate from the top of the head and white tooth-like shapes protrude below the red circles, concentrating the most saturated warm colors into that small upper-right zone.
reading: The figure's stretched limbs pull in opposite directions, giving the image a sense of imbalance — readable as mid-fall or mid-reach. Orange and blue compete across the same surface without either winning. The red circles and bared teeth compress intensity into a small area, while the rest of the body stays open and angular. That contrast between a dense, charged head and a sparse, spread body gives the whole image an uneasy charge.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work's teal ground also appears in the separate nifty-faces collection — a connection the collector reads across nnxyz's work. Title neighbors in the owned nnotb subset are nnotb #17 and nnotb #19.

connections.reason: Both works share the same flat teal ground and use white line to outline forms against it, though nifty faces #117 compresses everything into a close-up head while nnotb #18 spreads a single figure across open space.

Both nnotb #17 and nnotb #18 show a standing figure with arms extended wide, but #17 uses a muted olive ground with pink-red lines, making the shift to teal and orange in #18 a strong color contrast between these title neighbors.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye settle first — the dense cluster of spikes, teeth, and red circles at the head, or the wide arc of the outstretched arm — and what does that path through the image do to how you read the figure's posture?
ambiguities: The recorded creation order and title order align for this work, but the metadata notes gaps and variants may exist elsewhere in the nnotb family, so neither order should be read as a complete sequence.
nnotb #19 was inspected but its densely layered multi-figure composition offers no single strong formal parallel to #18's isolated figure, so it was not selected as a connection.
